condition.narrative: Legal Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.B: The Borrower shall cause the PIE to; (i) ensure that the Project is carried out withdue regard to appropriate health, safety, social, and environmental practices and standards, and in accordance with the SafeguardDocuments; and (ii) refrain from taking any action which would prevent or interfere with the implementation of the SafeguardDocuments, including any amendment, suspension, waiver, annulment and/or voidance of any provision of the Safeguard Documents,whether in whole or part, without the prior written concurrence of the Bank.

Legal Agreement: Schedule 2, Section II.The Borrower shall cause the PIE to prepare, under terms of reference satisfactory to theBank, and furnish to the Bank no later than thirty-six (36) months from the Effective Date, a consolidated mid-term review reportfor the Project, in accordance with the provision of paragraph 2 of Section II of the Schedule to the Project Agreement.

Project Agreement: Schedule, Section I. C.The PIE shall ensure that the Sub-projects do not include any activities or expenditureson the negative list set forth in the ESMF. Except as the Bank shall otherwise agree in writing, the PIE shall ensure, and causeto ensure, that none of the provisions of the Safeguard Documents be abrogated, amended, repealed, suspended or waived. In case ofany inconsistencies between the provisions of any of the Safeguard Documents and the provisions of this Agreement and/or the LoanAgreement the provisions of the latter agreement(s) shall prevail.

Project Agreement: Schedule, Section I.A.The PIE shall; (i) maintain throughout the period of Project implementation, the ProjectSteering Committee, with composition, resources and terms of reference acceptable to the Bank, to provide overall advice and policydirections for Project implementation and monitoring Project implementation; (ii) maintain throughout the period of Projectimplementation, the Project Management Unit (“PMU”), set up within the WBTIDCL, headed by a Project Director assisted by competentstaff, all with experience and qualifications, in numbers and under terms of reference agreed with the Bank.

Project Agreement: Schedule, Section II.The PIE shall (i) monitor and evaluate the progress of the Project and prepare ProjectReports on the basis of indicators acceptable to the Bank, covering the period of one calendar semester, and shall be furnished tothe Bank not later than forty-five days after the end of the period covered by such report; and (ii) prepare, under terms ofreference satisfactory to the Bank, and furnish to the Bank no later than thirty-six (36) months from the Effective Date, aconsolidated mid-term review report for the Project, summarizing the results of the monitoring and evaluation activities carriedout from the inception of the Project, and setting out the measures recommended to ensure the efficient completion of the Projectand to further its objective.

Project Agreement: Schedule, Section III.(i) The PIE shall maintain, throughout Project implementation, and publicize theavailability of a grievance redress mechanism, in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank, to hear and determine fairly and ingood faith all complaints raised in relation to the Project and take all measures necessary to implement the determinations made bysuch mechanism in a manner satisfactory to the Bank,(ii) Without limitation to the provision of paragraph 1 above, no later thanone month after the Effective Date, the PIE shall establish a functional web-based grievance redress mechanism, in form andsubstance satisfactory to the Bank.

comment.narrative: Following the initial assessment, two Origin–Destination pairs were identified for evaluating the feasibility of Ro-Ro terminals: Shalimar–GR Jetty and Kukrahati–Raichak. • Kukrahati–Raichak: The feasibility study prepared by Jadavpur University is yet to be finalized. Although the report has undergone two rounds of review, the revised version still lacks a comprehensive feasibility assessment. Preparation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR) and tender documents is currently in progress. • Shalimar–GR Jetty: The feasibility study prepared by IIEST Shibpur is not finalized and was under review by the Bank team. The bank team shared the feedback on the report and concerns on the condition for land availability arrangement.

Kukrahati-Raichak is the priority route selected for this indicator Jadavpur University is preparing a feasibility report for the Ro-Ro (Roll-on/Roll-off) service for this route, which includes various site-related surveys along with social and environmental assessments. In parallel, JU is also working on the draft Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) and Request for Bids (RFB), which are scheduled to be submitted by the end of June 2025. Tendering and on-boarding of Contractor for the works is expected by September 2025 for a construction period of 24 months. Completion of civil works is expected by October 2027.

title.narrative: Percentage passenger volume increase on selected ferry routes between Kolkata and Howrah and additional priority routes (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative:
Target achieved. The overall passenger volume increase for all seven routes is 45.7%. Baseline - 25,864 and current - 37,690.
Passenger volume between Kolkata and Howrah are: 1)Howrah – Fairlie: Baseline: 3200, Current – 5680 2)Howrah – Shipping: Baseline: 3100, Current – 4928 3)Howrah – Chandpal: Baseline: 3300, Current – 4046 4)Howrah – Armenian: Baseline: 2664, Current –3139 The volume increase based on these routes is 45%.
The volume on three additional priority routes are: 5) Chinsurah - Naihati: Baseline - 5500, Current - 8084 6) Sheoraphuli - Manirampur: Baseline - 5500, Current - 7801 7) Konnagar - Panihati - 2600 , Current - 4012
The slight reduction in the passenger volume since the last survey date is due to seasonal variation but overall the passenger volume has increased compared to the baseline.
Data source: Baseline - ISDP 2018 EY report sample head count; Current – Jadavpur University consultant survey reports

title.narrative: Percent complaints resolved of the total complaints received using the dedicated helpline number and internet-based communication tools to report sexual harassment and GBV issues

target.value: At least 80 percent resolved out of total complaints received.

comment.narrative:
Target achieved. Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) approved; email reporting system & dedicated helpline in place. The website and GRM portal are working on private server. All the complaints received have been resolved.
In addition to the above, the Government of West Bengal operates its own Public Grievance Redressal and Monitoring System (PGMS). Most complaints are routed through PGMS, and departments such as the Transport Department, West Bengal Transport, WBTIDCL, West Bengal Transport Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited, and West Bengal Surface Transport Corporation are already onboarded onto the system. Each department has a designated Nodal Officer responsible for monitoring and addressing complaints pertaining to their respective departments. All complaints received through PGMS are required to be resolved within a maximum of 30 days. The Department of Planning and Statistics is dedicated to managing and maintaining this system.

actual.value: Grievance Redress Mechanism in place and operational. 100 percent resolution rate.

title.narrative: Percent complaints resolved of the total complaints received using the dedicated helpline number and internet-based communication tools to report sexual harassment and GBV issues

target.value: At least 80 percent resolved out of total complaints received.

comment.narrative:
Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) approved; email reporting system & dedicated helpline in place. The website and GRM portal are working on private server. All the complaints received have been resolved.
In addition to the above, the Government of West Bengal operates its own Public Grievance Redressal and Monitoring System (PGMS). Most complaints are routed through PGMS, and departments such as the Transport Department, WBTIDCL, WBTC, and WBSTC are already onboarded onto the system. Each department has a designated Nodal Officer responsible for monitoring and addressing complaints pertaining to their respective departments. All complaints received through PGMS are required to be resolved within a maximum of 30 days. The Department of Planning and Statistics is dedicated to managing and maintaining this system.

actual.value: Grievance Redress Mechanism in place and operational. 100 percent resolution rate.
